chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hamzah ibn Ya'la from Zakariyya ibn Adam from al-Kahili who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the day of doubt in the month of Sha'ban. He said: 'Fasting one day from Sha'ban is more beloved to me than if I were to break the fast for one day from the month of Ramadan.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan, the ninth month of fasting
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: The day of doubt, referring to the 30th of Sha'ban when the moon is not sighted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the day of doubt in Sha'ban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the virtue of precaution (*ihtiyat*) by stating that fasting a day of doubt in Sha'ban is more beloved to him than breaking a fast in Ramadan, thereby encouraging believers to secure the validity of the obligatory month. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle of treating the 'day of doubt' as a probable day of Ramadan, ensuring the fulfillment of the divine command even in the absence of definitive lunar sighting. The preference for fasting over breaking highlights the gravity of missing an obligatory fast, reinforcing the importance of vigilance in religious observance.
